title: Reconstruction-independent moment tests for sample-based spectral functions — reproduction repository
description:
Reproduction deposit for N. Bonilla Vargas, What low-order sum rules can and cannot detect in sample-based spectral functions (deposit 2.0.3, 2026-11-17; earlier versions of the deposit accompany earlier versions of the manuscript, titled Reconstruction-independent moment tests for sample-based spectral functions). It contains the exact sector-Lanczos/Haydock engine and every generator behind the quoted numbers and figures, the deposited data (one dated JSON per computation), the hash-sealed pre-registrations and records of the blinded test and of the on-device nk test (which submitted no device job), the raw counts and submitted circuits of the IBM Quantum (ibm_fez) jobs, verification scripts with a record check (python src/verify.py), Makefile targets and a notebook that run the generators. Version 2.0.3 adds the Krylov detection-order analysis (src/krylov_detection_order.py) and the tie-order scan of the operator-form example (src/operator_form_tie_scan.py), with their data; the files of the manuscript's Fig. 5 and Table SII with the two programs that write the data files of Fig. 5 and the rows of Table SII; and the folder paper_2026-11/, with the sources of the present manuscript and three scripts that check printed numbers of that text against the deposited records. Every moment in the work is evaluated classically; the device supplies only sampled supports. What does not regenerate exactly from source is listed in docs/REPRODUCE.md (Known gaps). Code under the MIT licence; manuscript, data and documentation under CC BY 4.0; third-party LaTeX template files keep their own terms.

Summary of the work. Sample-based quantum diagonalization reconstructs dynamical spectral functions in sampled determinant subspaces, and moments read off such a reconstruction agree with it by construction. The work determines what low-order sum-rule checks can and cannot detect in these spectra. Full-operator moments of the probe, evaluated on the subspace ground state, differ from the reconstruction's moments exactly by the leak of the probe state out of the subspace, order by order, so that a pipeline can test the closure of its own output. The textbook double-commutator form lacks this property. With exact moments plus shot noise, the first and second moments detect weight moved in frequency at fixed total weight. Through m2 no check has guaranteed power against weight redistributed among four or more fixed poles, and, by the classical Gauss-quadrature property of the Lanczos recursion, an n-node reconstruction is invisible below order 2n, with a first residual bounded by an elementary Chebyshev–Jensen estimate.
